annotations.title: Check a document while you work on it

description: Prints a document only to check it — the person sees nothing: no PDF link, no card, nothing counted to their plan's pages. Answers with its pages as pictures, which heading starts on which page (outline), what runs past the paper, fonts not found, the tag tree a screen reader gets, the standards the file declares and, where the account's plan includes it, veraPDF's report on the standard it declares (PDF/UA-1, PDF/UA-2 or PDF/A-3a): each rule that fails, with its pages. For trying a layout, finding where a part lands and fixing what the validator finds; the person gets the document from render_pdf, render_template or update_document.

document_id.description: Or a document by its link (or its edit link), as it is now: its source, data and standards.

html.description: The whole HTML document to check, as render_pdf takes it.

options.description: The engine's print options — the same as the ReflowPDF API's `options` (https://api.reflowpdf.com/docs/), each checked the same way: a wrong or conflicting one is refused with what to change. Shrinking like a browser's print: shrink_to_fit (fit to the page width) or print_scale (a factor, e.g. 0.8 for 80%). pdf_ua, pdf_a and shrink_to_fit may also be given outside options. Given with document_id: they replace the document's for this check.

allow_remote.description: Fetch remote images, stylesheets and fonts over http(s) (public addresses only). `false` renders with embedded resources only.

attachments.description: Files to embed in the PDF (10 MB in total). With `pdf_a: "3a"` they are PDF/A-3 associated files. Not allowed with `pdf_a: "1b"` or `pdf_x`, whose standards forbid embedded files.

description.description: A description shown by PDF readers.

element.description: The `id` of the element the file belongs to (e.g. a table's data); the whole document if omitted.

relationship.description: The file's relationship to the document (PDF/A-3 `AFRelationship`).

base_css.description: Your CSS, applied at the user-agent level: defaults that the document's own CSS can override.

base_url.description: The base URL (http or https) for the document's relative URLs; acts as `<base href>` unless the document sets its own.

color_scheme.description: The value of the `prefers-color-scheme` media feature.

compression.description: Lossless compression effort for streams. Images are never resampled.

default_font_size.description: The size of CSS `medium`: the document's base font size.

e_invoice.description: Produce a hybrid e-invoice: Factur-X 1.0 / ZUGFeRD 2.5 (FNFE-MPE and FeRD, Factur-X 1.09.2), a PDF/A-3a with the invoice XML embedded. The XML is validated against its profile first (the KoSIT validator for XRechnung 3.0; the EN 16931 XSD and Schematron of Factur-X 1.09.2); an invoice that fails is refused with each violated rule. Its `attachments` use the formats Factur-X allows (§6.4: PDF, TXT, GIF, TIFF, JPG, CSV, XML, JSON, XLS, XLSX, ODS, each with its `mime_type`) and names other than the invoice's (`factur-x.xml`, `xrechnung.xml`, `zugferd-invoice.xml`). Not with `pdf_a: "1b"`, `pdf_ua: 2`, `pdf_x`, `wtpdf` or `encryption`. An e-invoice depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

profile.description: `en16931`: the EN 16931 (Comfort) profile, embedded as `factur-x.xml`; `xrechnung`: the XRECHNUNG reference profile (the German CIUS), embedded as `xrechnung.xml`. The XML's specification identifier (BT-24) must match the profile exactly: `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017`, or `urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:xeinkauf.de:kosit:xrechnung_3.0` (XRechnung 3.0).

xml.description: The invoice as UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice (CII) XML text, up to 5 MB in UTF-8. It is embedded as UTF-8, so its XML declaration must specify UTF-8 or no encoding.

encryption.description: Encrypt the PDF (AES-256 by default, ISO 32000-2). Not compatible with PDF/A or PDF/X, whose standards forbid encryption.

algorithm.description: Use `rc4-128` only for readers older than Acrobat 9.

owner_password.description: The password that lifts the permission restrictions.

permissions.description: Allowed actions; anything not listed is denied. Text extraction for accessibility (screen readers) is always allowed (ISO 32000-2, PDF/UA).

user_password.description: The password required to open the file. If empty or omitted, the file opens without a password, with the permissions below.

header_footer.description: A line of text in the top and bottom margins of every page. CSS `@page` margin boxes (`@top-center { content: … counter(page) }`) do the same in the document itself, with full styling.

footer.description: Text in the bottom margin of every page; `{pageNum}` and `{totalPages}` are replaced.

header.description: `{pageNum}` and `{totalPages}` are replaced on each page.

javascript.description: Run the document's scripts before rendering, against the engine's own DOM, with layout queries answered by the engine. Off by default: without it scripts do not run.

lang.description: The document language (BCP 47), used when `<html lang>` is not set.

max_pages.description: Render at most this many pages; the rest is omitted.

object_streams.description: Pack objects into object streams (smaller files). `false` writes a classic cross-reference table for readers older than PDF 1.5.

paper.description: The default paper, applied as a user-agent `@page` rule: any property the document's own `@page` sets takes precedence. Without either: A4 portrait, 20 mm margins.

size.description: A0–A10, B0–B10, C0–C10, JIS-B4, JIS-B5, Letter, Legal, Ledger, Tabloid, or two lengths such as "210mm 297mm".

pdf_a.description: Declare PDF/A conformance: `3a` is ISO 19005-3, conformance level A (tagged, includes PDF/UA-1); `1b` is ISO 19005-1, conformance level B (PDF 1.4: transparency is flattened into opaque images, text stays selectable). A document that cannot conform is refused with the reason. PDF/A depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

pdf_ua.description: Declare PDF/UA conformance: `1` (ISO 14289-1, PDF 1.7) or `2` (ISO 14289-2, PDF 2.0). Every PDF is tagged unless `tagged: false`. PDF/UA-2 depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

pdf_x.description: Declare PDF/X conformance for an output intent: colors, page boxes and the output intent of a print-ready file. PDF/X depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

output_intent.description: A print condition of the engine's registry (e.g. `FOGRA39`, `CGATS21-2-CRPC5`, `CGATS TR 001`), or the name of your own `profile`.

profile.description: Your printer's ICC output profile (device class `prtr`; Gray, RGB or CMYK; up to 8 MB), base64-encoded.

standard.description: `x-4`: ISO 15930-7 (PDF 1.6, transparency and RGB preserved); `x-1a`: ISO 15930-4 (PDF 1.4, all colors converted to the output intent's inks, transparency flattened; requires a CMYK output intent).

print_scale.description: Scale the document down by this factor.

shrink_to_fit.description: Scale a document wider than the page down to fit, as browsers do. Off by default, so lengths stay physical.

tagged.description: Produce a tagged PDF (logical structure for screen readers and reflow). `false` produces a smaller untagged file; not compatible with `pdf_ua` or `pdf_a: "3a"`.

title.description: The PDF title (defaults to the document's `<title>`, then to its first `<h1>`).

watermark.description: A text or image stamped on every page, behind the content unless `above` is set; marked as an artifact in a tagged PDF.

above.description: Draw over the content instead of behind it.

image.description: An https or data: URL of an image (instead of `text`).

image_width.description: Image width in points, with `image_height` (defaults to its natural size at 96 dpi).

position.description: Place a single stamp at this position (points from the page's top-left corner) instead of the center.

tile.description: Repeat the stamp across the page.

tile_spacing.description: [x, y] spacing of the tiles, in points.

wtpdf.description: Declare Well-Tagged PDF 1.0 conformance (PDF Association): a tagged PDF 2.0 that declares its conformance level. `accessibility` declares both levels (it includes the requirements of `reuse`); `reuse` declares the reuse level. The file also conforms to PDF/UA-2. Not with `pdf_a`, `pdf_x` or `pdf_ua: 1`, which use earlier PDF versions. Well-Tagged PDF depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

pdf_a.description: Declare PDF/A: "3a" — ISO 19005-3 level A, tagged, includes PDF/UA-1 (archive and accessibility at once); "1b" — ISO 19005-1 level B (PDF 1.4: transparency flattened into images). A document that cannot conform is refused with the reason. PDF/A depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

pdf_ua.description: The PDF/UA part the file declares: 1 (ISO 14289-1, PDF 1.7) — every print declares it; 2 (ISO 14289-2, PDF 2.0). Not with pdf_a. PDF/UA-2 depends on the account's plan; a print it does not include is refused with the reason.

preview_pages.description: Which pages to see, 1-based; -1 is the last page. Default: page 1 and the last. Pick them by the outline of an earlier answer.

shrink_to_fit.description: Print a document wider than its page smaller, to fit, as a browser's print does: every length then prints scaled down. Default: false, lengths print at their size (20mm is 20mm). Prefer fitting the layout to the page; use this for a page made for a screen.

tags.description: The tag tree in the answer. Default: true.

name: check_document

missingFonts.description: Font families the document named that no face answered: their text took the next family of its list.

notes.description: Facts about this PDF: how long its link works, its mark, what was not fetched or filled.

outline.description: The document's headings (h1–h6, the PDF's bookmarks) in order, each with the page it starts on: pick preview_pages by it.

preview.description: Which pages came with this answer as pictures (PNG), or why none did.

skippedResources.description: Images, fonts or style sheets the server could not fetch.

standards.description: What the PDF declares, read from its file: pdfUa (its PDF/UA part) and pdfA (its PDF/A part and level, e.g. "3a"), null when it declares none.

tags.description: The tag tree a screen reader gets: text (each element and its text, indented), lines, cut (when longer than shown).

validation.description: veraPDF on the standard the file declares (by the account's plan): profile, compliant, and the rules that fail — id (the standard's clause and test), title, plain (what it means for a reader), priority, count, pages; gated: true where the plan does not include it; error: why it could not run.
